findings.finding: The diagnostic runtime is v22.23.2; installed root and snapshot declarations are @types/node 25.6.0, not Node22 declarations. Their LookupFunction accepts string | LookupAddress[] and optional family, and LookupOptions exposes all. The proposed two callback forms fit those inspected declarations without any or an unchecked cast.
findings.disposition: Accept the proposed shape on static evidence plus the recorded Node22 API control. Future Node22 execution and typecheck remain mandatory; no dependency/lockfile correction is authorized by this slice.

findings.finding: Literal-host controls exercise HTTP/Response behavior, not lookup pinning: the native literal-host connect path can bypass lookup. In guarded composition, a literal URL produces that same literal as resolvedAddresses[0]. Direct callers supplying a mismatched literal URL/address are outside the guard invariant and were not qualified.
findings.disposition: Use synthetic hostname .invalid for the pinning/DNS acceptance in both lookup modes. Do not transfer literal-loopback controls into arbitrary direct-call pinning guarantees, guard permission or real-provider proof. No guard or literal-routing redesign is required by this bounded correction.

findings.finding: A direct transport Response304 must have body=null and ok=false. The unchanged shared caller treats every 3xx as a redirect; with no Location it rejects, and model callers set maxRedirects=0. Thus transport304 conformance does not promise a public provider returns304 successfully.
findings.disposition: Preserve the existing caller behavior and adapter error classification. This SPEC explicitly limits bodyless conformance to the transport and does not authorize a redirect-contract change.

findings.finding: V1 ends with exit1 and no serialized observations when the channel localhost constructor rejects blocked_hostname. V2's two model cases call nonexistent complete, make zero requests and zero DNS calls; neither is public model behavior evidence. Its channel200 acceptance and channel204 send_failed/effectUnknown=true after one request each are valid recorded synthetic observations. V3 calls actual ModelProvider.execute and independently records the model and channel observations described below.
findings.disposition: Preserve V1/V2 invalid harness history; use V3 only for its actual synthetic public boundaries. The SPEC's line11 limits the linked direct probes and remains true; supplemental public synthetic data strengthens confidence in observable impact without changing the normative SPEC or granting real integration/BUILD authority.

assessments.conclusion: The original transport JSON has 12 observations, 10 server requests, fixtureClosed=true, two hostname GET200 rejections, six GET204/205/304 constructor rejections, two HEAD200 responses with non-null body, and two empty GET200 controls with non-null body. Baseline classifies exactly these cases as 10 FAIL and 2 PASS. The original Node API control records all=true for default-family requests, one existing-format rejection, and two reference successes including legacy single-result mode with agent:false. Reference success is not corrected-product execution.

assessments.conclusion: Both current transports overwrite caller Host with url.host and use original hostname for HTTP authority and HTTPS servername. The proposed correction leaves these intact. A child-only synthetic CA, SAN hostname, observed SNI/Host, hostname-mismatch and untrusted-CA negatives provide appropriate future TLS acceptance without changing system trust.
assessments.requiredFutureEvidence: The positive must validate trusted SAN/hostname and preserve original SNI; each negative must isolate its intended validation failure. These fixtures have not yet run.

assessments.conclusion: Passing the effective Node request method and using null for HEAD/head and final204/205/304 directly addresses the recorded failures. Empty GET200 retains its body; status/headers/ok distinctions and adapter classification remain unchanged. Existing readResponse consumes IncomingMessage to completion; request and stream errors flow through the existing single-settlement wrapper. The SPEC forbids settlement while leaving a discarded stream/socket pending.
assessments.requiredFutureEvidence: Assert body identity as well as text and status; observe wire method for lowercase head. Event-driven pre-abort, in-flight abort, connection failure and response-stream failure must prove rejection and socket cleanup. Exercise response draining and failure during reading; a fulfilled status assertion alone is insufficient.

No new package, lockfile, guard, exports, shared refactor or global DNS/TLS setting is permitted. The UP91 transport preparation claim is active and the earlier test-only lane is interrupted. Integration, commits, push and release require their own coordination and applicable authority; this review performs none.

limitations: This review inspected local files, source declarations and stored diagnostic JSON only. It ran no product tests, diagnostic reruns, network operations, installs, PostgreSQL, certification or subagents.
The proposed correction is not implemented in the inspected sources. Planned acceptance tests, TLS/IPv6/encoding/pinning/abort/stream cases and full gates are NOT_RUN by this reviewer.
Recorded probe exit0 means the diagnostic finished, not product PASS. Cleanup is historical evidence from the probe output and source; this reviewer did not inspect live sockets or rerun cleanup.

The transport probe exposes an aggregate request counter, not per-case network traces. Attribution of pre-request hostname rejection combines recorded outcomes, aggregate10/12, source and the separate Node API control.
Current hashes and raw/observed equality establish local consistency. No external immutable seal, execution attestation or original run authenticity was independently verified.
Installed declarations are for Node25; type shape inspection does not replace behavioral verification on the required Node22 runtime, and this slice cannot change dependencies.
Direct loopback fixtures bypass shared guard/caller composition and establish no real provider/channel permission, qualification, delivery, retry/budget guarantees or productive readiness.
Concurrent writers can change inputs after review. Revalidate the exact SPEC/source hashes and claims before relying on this report for a human decision or later BUILD.
